title: Gmail read-only: MCP path
description: Scripted walkthrough of the official Gmail MCP setup and read-only test. No Google login or mailbox access occurs in playback.

commands: # In Google Cloud: enable Gmail API and Gmail MCP API
# Create an agent-enabled OAuth Web client
# In Google's OAuth Playground: request only gmail.readonly
# Save the agent's remote MCP configuration from the tutorial
( IFS= read -rs CS357_GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN && export CS357_GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN && opencode )
# Ask the agent for one search_threads call
# Close the agent and revoke the test application's Google access

markers.title: Set up a preview project
markers.note: The MCP API requires Google Workspace Developer Preview access. If you cannot enable it, choose the CLI path.

markers.title: Register the OAuth client
markers.note: Use Google's OAuth Playground as the redirect. Add only Gmail read access to Data Access.

markers.title: Verify the grant
markers.note: Choose Online access and check the scope in Google's token response. No authorization or token is shown here.

markers.title: Configure the connection
markers.note: Use Google's Gmail MCP endpoint. The configuration references an environment variable; it contains no token.

markers.title: Start the agent
markers.note: Bash/Zsh illustration. The page also has a masked PowerShell example. Paste a token only into the real hidden terminal prompt, never into chat.

markers.title: Check the connection
markers.note: In Oh My Pi, use /mcp test gmail-demo and /tools. The catalog alone does not establish your OAuth permissions.

markers.title: Test with a Read-Only Request
markers.note: Use the demo subject, pageSize 3, and THREAD_VIEW_IDS_ONLY. Check the tool trace and count only the first page. This playback does not read a mailbox.

markers.title: Clean up
markers.note: Close the Playground and clear the clipboard. The short-lived token is no longer in the terminal environment after the agent exits.
